analysis: This PR is documentation-only. It changes docs/architecture/inference.md (Flint section, head lines 2058-2073) and docs/developer/test.md (line 918). The documented behavior changes are: Flint is paged-only; an automatic KV backend selection is treated as explicit paged; a contiguous selection, the paged kill switch or a capability veto refuses the load; and EngineV2KVQuantizationPolicy.resolve ignores provider-wide defaults for Flint but refuses an explicit non-native per-model or environment selection. The test doc now says DARKBLOOM_FLINT_BACKEND may only be unset or paged. These are fail-closed refusals, so I found no weakening of the model-load, prefix-cache, attestation or encryption controls. I checked the cache threat entry T-041 against the changed text. The doc changes do not alter SSD tier gating, TTL, HMAC lookup tags or salt scoping, so the T-041 mitigations are unaffected. Paged attention does change which KV and prefix-cache path Flint uses, so the paged prefix-cache and SSD tier behavior for Flint deserves review where the code lands. I did not see that implementation; it is outside the supplied evidence. The unchanged surrounding text covers coordinator-serving channels, withheld reasoning, tool constraints and MiMo. It claims no new endpoints, no new trust grants and no catalog or release activation. I did not independently verify those claims against code. Remaining question: whether the code behind these docs (EngineV2Factory.prepareProductionBackend, EngineV2KVQuantizationPolicy.resolve) matches the documented refusal semantics. That belongs to code review, not to this docs-only change, and it cannot be settled from the supplied evidence.
